findings.criterion: 4 — a ChatGPT terminal is opened from the dashboard and its greet is seen on the page (Playwright screenshot), not inferred from a stub
findings.section: Wave 7 — live Playwright sign-off and v1.2.12 ship gate
findings.message: The only non-stub proof is skippable (`pytest.importorskip('playwright')` plus `ANCHOR_TESTS_ALLOW_LIVE=1` plus a real `codex` binary). A skip is a green pytest. The wait is for unnamed "Codex greet text." The tag rule is "the screenshot file exists" plus the stub suite. A blank xterm, a login wall, an on-request approval modal, a throwaway-port harness that is not `:8777`, or a planted PNG all satisfy "file exists." Criterion 4 is a claim about John's dashboard page. The warm-restart sentence in done-when is a ritual with no named string and is not in the tag condition. As written, v1.2.12 can ship with the greet still inferred.

findings.criterion: 1 — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
findings.section: Wave 7 live test / Wave 3 seed timing
findings.message: The dashboard action W7 clicks is "Open terminal," a bare `general` session — historically no lane skill. Playwright then waits for unnamed Codex chrome and records `seed_delivery`, which is not the skill loading. W3's stub done-when is `seeded True` on PTY *input*; the greet is *output* and is never asserted on research/plan/build. W7 does not fail if `seed_delivery` is `stdin-timeout-fallback` or if the skill text never appears in the buffer. Criterion 1 is a seeded trio cockpit, not a banner in an empty general box. An operator who then starts Research/Plan/Build on ChatGPT is running the unproven path. The stub "seed written" and the live button do not even agree on which lane is the proof.

findings.criterion: 2 — picker shows "ChatGPT — ready"; a host without the Codex binary still fails closed; risk table — picker shows "unavailable" there
findings.message: W1 sets `selectable=True`, `status='ready'`, and a static reason "Codex CLI detected…" with no detection. Tests pin "no seat is disabled." The only absent-binary GWT is `start_session` raising `chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing` — after the operator has already been told the seat is ready and detected. The North Star already chose the operator-visible mitigation: the picker says unavailable. This draft implements the opposite lie, and the "no seat is disabled" pin forbids fixing it.

findings.criterion: 2 — the Terminal picker shows "ChatGPT — ready" AND 1 — PTY running the Codex TUI with `--cd`, `--no-alt-screen`, `-s workspace-write`
findings.section: Wave 1 done-when vs Wave 2 launch argv
findings.message: W1's definition of done is the picker and capability note saying ready, while the launch is still bare `codex` (alt-screen, no `--cd`, no sandbox) until W2. That is the operator-visible surface going green before the terminal can open as specified. Every wave "ships real source" onto a live service. A mid-effort restart, or a saved `default_cli=chatgpt` after W1, presents a first-class seat that hits the exact alt-screen failure the risk table named. "Ready" is a surface claim, not a permission to open a gate.

findings.criterion: 1 — POST /api/rnd/term_set_engine switches a live session to and from ChatGPT; the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
findings.section: Wave 3 — seed timing / Wave 2 switch_engine relaunch sites
findings.message: First-output-gated seed is specified for `start_session` at the stdin site. Engine switch is the operator's other way onto ChatGPT (criterion 1 names it). W2 applies launch argv at both relaunch sites; W3 does not apply `SEED_AFTER_FIRST_OUTPUT_BACKENDS` there. Toggling Claude → ChatGPT can dump the skill into a composer that is not up — the seed-before-ready risk, on the hotter operator path. W7 asserts `len(pty_manager.live_sessions())` unchanged after toggle, not that the ChatGPT side was seeded after first output or that a greet is visible after the switch.

findings.criterion: 1 — approvals left to the user in the terminal; risk table — seed must not land before the TUI is ready, nor as an approval
findings.message: On timeout the plan still writes the seed ("never a silently unseeded live session"). That is how a login wall or on-request approval becomes the seed's target — the operator's first keystrokes answer Codex, or the skill is submitted as the approval. The immediately-emitting stub never takes this path; live Codex is the path that will. The draft also refuses to inject `-a` and treats "no flag" as "on-request," which is an assumption about v0.151 defaults, not a pin. Criterion 1's approval contract is unenforced on the path most likely to fire on a real open.

findings.criterion: 3 — session usage state is uncorrelated; any rollup that includes it is stamped partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured) — never an mtime guess, never a fabricated $0.00
findings.message: The draft asserts three stamps at once: empty `stored_engine_uuid` → finalize `uncorrelated`; `usage_unmeasured_segments` + `classify_session_usage` "measured + any segment → STATE_PARTIAL"; and "ended on chatgpt with no reason is stamped chatgpt-segment." The operator-facing badge is then whichever branch wins. Criterion 3 split session vs rollup on purpose. As written, a ChatGPT-start session can show as partial, or a rollup can inherit a session-level reason. The done-when names "the dashboard rollup badge," but every GWT inspects `classify_session_usage` / the record — not the widget John reads — so a leftover `$0.00` on the page would still ship.

findings.criterion: 3 — live_doctor_session(backend="chatgpt") launches with -s read-only
findings.message: The function is stub-tested. John does not call `live_doctor_session`. W4 never says how Diagnose chooses ChatGPT — `default_cli`, a picker, or a hidden argument. If Diagnose stays on Claude (or on a write-posture default), the read-only Codex Doctor never appears on the surface criterion 3 is for. A stub argv walk is not Doctor-capable in the cockpit.

findings.criterion: 1 — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives; approvals left to the user in the terminal
findings.message: W7's ship escape hatch is `codex '<seed>'` as the first argv prompt if stdin-after-first-output fails live. The North Star's own TUI form is `codex [PROMPT]` — that prompt is the first turn, not a pending paste. The fallback therefore auto-submits the skill as Codex's opening task, which is the opposite of "approvals stay on-request for the user to answer in the terminal" and the opposite of Grok-style stdin-after-first-output. The plan already expects the primary seed path to fail on John's screen, then ships the auto-submit path with "its own stub test" and no live fail if that is what actually ran.

findings.criterion: 3 — the session's usage state is uncorrelated and any rollup that includes it is stamped partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured); never an mtime guess, never a fabricated $0.00
findings.message: Criterion 3 requires two stamps at once. The wave then specifies a classifier that cannot emit them together. `classify_session_usage` is `measured + any segment → STATE_PARTIAL`; a chatgpt-START session is `stored_engine_uuid == ''` so the W4 finalize path yields `uncorrelated`; and “ended on chatgpt with no reason is stamped chatgpt-segment.” Those are three different states. A session that is not `measured` never enters the `measured + segment` arm, so the same wave’s done-when — `rnd rollup` and the dashboard badge reading `partial (chatgpt segment unmeasured)` — does not fire for the chatgpt-only project the North Star named. The leftover “chatgpt-segment” rule would overwrite `uncorrelated` with `partial` to make the badge green. Either the session stamp is a lie, or the rollup stamp is silent. That is the hole Option C was ruled to close: a builder who needs a green badge will enter the mtime/cwd-window path or write `$0.00`. W5 names `UNMEASURED_SEGMENT_BACKENDS` and a test that “no cost number is written,” but it never identifies which function emits which stamp, nor what `classify_session_usage` returns for an uncorrelated chatgpt-only project, nor does it separate empty (no ChatGPT session, rollup fully measured) from unknown (ledger unreadable) from uncorrelated (ChatGPT present, unmeasured). Until that state machine is one table with one test per stamp, criterion 3 is not implementable without fabricating a number or dropping the partial marker.

findings.criterion: 1 — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives; 4 — the greet is seen on the page, not inferred from a stub
findings.section: Wave 7 — live Playwright sign-off / Wave 3 seed
findings.message: The live test clicks dashboard “Open terminal” (a bare `general` session, historically no lane skill), waits for unnamed “Codex greet text,” and records `seed_delivery`. Criterion 1’s greet is the lane-skill greet after the seed, not TUI chrome (“OpenAI Codex”, a spinner, a login widget). Those are different dependent variables. A shot of Codex chrome can exist while the seed was dropped, eaten by an approval prompt, or never written — and `seed_delivery='stdin-timeout-fallback'` records the attempt, not arrival. W3 already sets `seeded=True` after `_pty.write` on a stub that emits immediately, so CI cannot falsify this. The live button and the stub done-when do not even agree on which lane is the proof. An operator who then starts Research/Plan/Build on ChatGPT is running the unproven path.

findings.criterion: 2 — picker shows “ChatGPT — ready”; a host without the Codex binary still fails closed; risk table — picker shows “unavailable” there
findings.message: Wave 1 sets `selectable=True`, `status='ready'`, and a static reason “Codex CLI detected…” with no `shutil.which` / resolver probe. Tests pin “no seat is disabled” and `'ChatGPT — ready' exactly once`. “Detected” is copy, not a measurement. Criterion 2’s happy path is therefore true even on a host with no `codex`, while the North Star’s own risk row required the picker to show unavailable and leave fail-closed to `chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing`. The plan implements only the resolver raise (and a test that the raise happens before a worktree). The user-visible truth table still says ready. A settings save of `default_cli=chatgpt` on that host then persists a lie that criterion 2 claimed the picker would not tell.

findings.criterion: 1 — lane seed written exactly once and the greet arrives; approvals left to the user; risk table — seed must not land before the TUI is ready, nor as an approval
findings.section: Wave 3 — first-output-gated seed / Wave 7 positional fallback
findings.message: The plan operationalizes “TUI ready” as “first PTY byte, else ~8s timeout then write anyway.” First output from Codex is not the composer; it is often banner, login, trust, or an approval widget. Writing the lane-skill seed into that widget is the failure mode the risk row named, and the timeout-fallback reintroduces seed-before-ready by design (“never leave unseeded”). The stub “emits output immediately,” which confounds the test: W3’s `seeded=True` / seed-once walk cannot fail this race. Approvals stay `on-request` is implemented by not passing `-a`; omission is not a pin of v0.151’s default. Wave 7 then parks a second, unconverged mechanism — `codex '<seed>'` as the first argv prompt — to be implemented if live already failed. A positional Codex prompt is the TUI’s first turn; that auto-submits the skill as the task, which is the opposite of “approvals left to the user” and “the seed only loads the skill and greets.” Two unmeasured seed paths plus a timeout write is not a mitigation.

findings.criterion: 1 — With default_cli=chatgpt (or the engine toggle), POST /api/rnd/term_start starts a PTY running the Codex TUI
findings.message: Criterion 1’s treatment is `default_cli=chatgpt` or the engine toggle driving `POST /api/rnd/term_start`. The plan proves persistence (`save_settings` / `get_default_cli`) and proves `start_session(..., backend='chatgpt')` when the backend is passed in. It never names the code that reads `get_default_cli()` (or the picker) inside `term_start` / the dashboard “Open terminal” button. Those are different independent variables. If Open terminal still uses `last_engine_for_project` or a hardcoded engine, Wave 1 can persist chatgpt and Wave 7 can set the setting, then click a button that starts Claude and wait for a Codex greet that will not come. “Why now” claimed only the allow-guard plus tables were closed; that is an assumption, not a traced call. Without a named consumer in a done-when, Foreman will not add the wiring.

findings.criterion: 3 — live_doctor_session(backend="chatgpt") launches with -s read-only (a DOCTOR_READONLY_CLI_ARGS entry)
findings.message: The argv contract is specified for a fresh stub `start_doctor_session`. The reuse contract is not: “a second `live_doctor_session(mode, backend='chatgpt', posture)` attaches to the keyed existing session.” If the live key is still `mode` (and maybe `posture`) without `backend`, Diagnose with ChatGPT attaches to an already-open Claude/Grok Doctor and never launches Codex, so the read-only table entry never appears on a PTY. Criterion 3 is the chatgpt Doctor launch, not “some Doctor is up.” `resolve=True` keeping `workspace-write` on the same session object makes a mode-only key even more likely to return the wrong engine with the wrong `-s`. No done-when asserts that a live non-chatgpt Doctor does not satisfy a `backend='chatgpt'` request, or that the Diagnose button actually passes `backend`. Stub argv on `start_doctor_session` does not measure `live_doctor_session`.

findings.criterion: 4 — the terminal nets stay green under the stub PTY; _LIVE_ENGINE_BASENAMES still refuses a real codex spawn; distro import scan stays clean
findings.message: The declared, machine-countable `test-command` is five files: `test_backend_chatgpt.py`, `test_anchor_settings.py`, `test_chatgpt_lane_routing.py`, `test_chatgpt_terminal_2026_09_05.py`, `test_model_switch_w7.py`. That is the Wave 1 subset plus one pre-existing switch test. It does not run `test_chatgpt_terminal_w2.py`, `w3`, `w4_doctor`, `test_chatgpt_accounting_w5.py`, `w6_net`, or the distro import-scan test Wave 6 names as the regression net. Criterion 4’s stub half is therefore not the command Foreman will count at ship. A green header gate can land with no argv pin, no seed-once pin, no Doctor `-s read-only` pin, no unmeasured-segment pin, and no live-engine refusal pin — every measure Waves 2–6 claimed would protect the surface.

findings.criterion: 1 — a terminal opens on ChatGPT with --cd worktree, --no-alt-screen, -s workspace-write; 4 — nothing regresses under ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub + ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD
findings.section: Wave 2 — argv order asserted under the stub
findings.message: The Codex TUI contract is the launch argv. CI is defined as `ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub` + `ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD`. Wave 2 asserts the stub PTY’s recorded argv is `[cmd, '--no-alt-screen', '-s', 'workspace-write', '--cd', worktree]` without saying the assertion reads the pre-replacement list `_interactive_launch_args` returns rather than the stub command that actually spawned. If `ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD` replaces the vector, W2’s new test is green while `ENGINE_LAUNCH_ARGS` never reaches a process, and Claude/Grok “byte-unchanged” pins do not protect the chatgpt branch. Criterion 1 then holds only in the skippable live test. Name the probe point or this is another stub-as-population result.

findings.section: Wave 7 — Live Playwright sign-off and the v1.2.12 ship gate
findings.criterion: 4 — before v1.2.12 ships a ChatGPT terminal is opened from the dashboard and its greet is seen on the page (Playwright screenshot), not inferred from a stub
findings.message: The only non-stub proof is skippable (`ANCHOR_TESTS_ALLOW_LIVE=1`) and the ship rule is “the screenshot file exists” plus “tag after the PNG exists.” No greet string is named. A blank xterm, a Codex login wall, an approval modal, TUI chrome, or a copied PNG all satisfy “file exists.” Criterion 4 is a claim about John’s page after a warm restart of the service he uses, not about a path on disk from a throwaway server on an OS-assigned port. The wave mixes those two surfaces and then gates the tag on the file. As written, v1.2.12 can ship with the greet still inferred — the exact failure the criterion forbade.

findings.topic: live greet oracle is Codex chrome not lane seed
findings.section: Wave 7 — live Playwright sign-off / Wave 3 seed
findings.criterion: 1 — the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives; 4 — the greet is seen on the page, not inferred from a stub
findings.message: The live test clicks dashboard “Open terminal” (a bare `general` session, historically no lane skill), waits for unnamed “Codex greet text,” and records `seed_delivery`. Criterion 1’s greet is the lane-skill greet after the seed, not TUI chrome (“OpenAI Codex”, a spinner, a login widget). Those are different dependent variables. A shot of Codex chrome can exist while the seed was dropped, eaten by an approval prompt, or never written — and `seed_delivery='stdin-timeout-fallback'` records the attempt, not arrival. W3 already sets `seeded=True` after `_pty.write` on a stub that emits immediately, so CI cannot falsify this. The live button and the stub done-when do not even agree on which lane is the proof. An operator who then starts Research/Plan/Build on ChatGPT is running the unproven path.

findings.criterion: 2 — picker shows “ChatGPT — ready”; a host without the Codex binary still fails closed; risk table — picker shows “unavailable” there
findings.message: Wave 1 sets `selectable=True`, `status='ready'`, and a static reason “Codex CLI detected…” with no `shutil.which` / resolver probe. Tests pin “no seat is disabled” and `'ChatGPT — ready' exactly once`. “Detected” is copy, not a measurement. Criterion 2’s happy path is therefore true even on a host with no `codex`, while the North Star’s own risk row required the picker to show unavailable and leave fail-closed to `chatgpt-terminal-binary-missing`. The plan implements only the resolver raise (and a test that the raise happens before a worktree). The user-visible truth table still says ready. A settings save of `default_cli=chatgpt` on that host then persists a lie that criterion 2 claimed the picker would not tell.

findings.section: Wave 1 done-when vs Wave 2 launch argv
findings.criterion: 2 — the Terminal picker shows “ChatGPT — ready”; 1 — PTY running the Codex TUI with `--cd`, `--no-alt-screen`, `-s workspace-write`
findings.message: Wave 1’s definition of done is the picker and capability note saying ready, while the launch is still bare `codex` (alt-screen, no `--cd`, no sandbox) until Wave 2. “Ready” is now a mergeable wave, not a later phase. Any mid-effort restart, or a saved `default_cli=chatgpt` after W1, presents a first-class seat that hits the exact alt-screen failure the risk table named. A surface claim cannot precede the launch contract it describes.

findings.topic: seed on first byte not composer-ready
findings.section: Wave 3 — first-output-gated seed / Wave 7 positional fallback
findings.criterion: 1 — lane seed written exactly once and the greet arrives; approvals left to the user; risk table — seed must not land before the TUI is ready, nor as an approval
findings.message: The plan operationalizes “TUI ready” as “first PTY byte, else ~8s timeout then write anyway.” First output from Codex is not the composer; it is often banner, login, trust, or an approval widget. Writing the lane-skill seed into that widget is the failure mode the risk row named, and the timeout-fallback reintroduces seed-before-ready by design (“never leave unseeded”). The stub “emits output immediately,” which confounds the test: W3’s `seeded=True` / seed-once walk cannot fail this race. Approvals stay `on-request` is implemented by not passing `-a`; omission is not a pin of v0.151’s default. Wave 7 then parks a second, unconverged mechanism — `codex '<seed>'` as the first argv prompt — to be implemented if live already failed. A positional Codex prompt is the TUI’s first turn; that auto-submits the skill as the task, which is the opposite of “approvals left to the user” and “the seed only loads the skill and greets.” Two unmeasured seed paths plus a timeout write is not a mitigation.

findings.criterion: 1 — With default_cli=chatgpt (or the engine toggle), POST /api/rnd/term_start starts a PTY running the Codex TUI
findings.message: Criterion 1’s treatment is `default_cli=chatgpt` or the engine toggle driving `POST /api/rnd/term_start`. The plan proves persistence (`save_settings` / `get_default_cli`) and proves `start_session(..., backend='chatgpt')` when the backend is passed in. It never names the code that reads `get_default_cli()` (or the picker) inside `term_start` / the dashboard “Open terminal” button. Those are different independent variables. If Open terminal still uses `last_engine_for_project` or a hardcoded engine, Wave 1 can persist chatgpt and Wave 7 can set the setting, then click a button that starts Claude and wait for a Codex greet that will not come. “Why now” claimed only the allow-guard plus tables were closed; that is an assumption, not a traced call. Without a named consumer in a done-when, Foreman will not add the wiring.

findings.criterion: 3 — live_doctor_session(backend="chatgpt") launches with -s read-only (a DOCTOR_READONLY_CLI_ARGS entry)
findings.message: The argv contract is specified for a fresh stub `start_doctor_session`. The reuse contract is not: “a second `live_doctor_session(mode, backend='chatgpt', posture)` attaches to the keyed existing session.” If the live key is still `mode` (and maybe `posture`) without `backend`, Diagnose with ChatGPT attaches to an already-open Claude/Grok Doctor and never launches Codex, so the read-only table entry never appears on a PTY. Criterion 3 is the chatgpt Doctor launch, not “some Doctor is up.” `resolve=True` keeping `workspace-write` on the same session object makes a mode-only key even more likely to return the wrong engine with the wrong `-s`. No done-when asserts that a live non-chatgpt Doctor does not satisfy a `backend='chatgpt'` request, or that the Diagnose button actually passes `backend`. Stub argv on `start_doctor_session` does not measure `live_doctor_session`.

findings.criterion: 4 — the terminal nets stay green under the stub PTY; _LIVE_ENGINE_BASENAMES still refuses a real codex spawn; distro import scan stays clean
findings.message: The declared, machine-countable `test-command` is five files: `test_backend_chatgpt.py`, `test_anchor_settings.py`, `test_chatgpt_lane_routing.py`, `test_chatgpt_terminal_2026_09_05.py`, `test_model_switch_w7.py`. That is the Wave 1 subset plus one pre-existing switch test. It does not run `test_chatgpt_terminal_w2.py`, `w3`, `w4_doctor`, `test_chatgpt_accounting_w5.py`, `w6_net`, or the distro import-scan test Wave 6 names as the regression net. Criterion 4’s stub half is therefore not the command Foreman will count at ship. A green header gate can land with no argv pin, no seed-once pin, no Doctor `-s read-only` pin, no unmeasured-segment pin, and no live-engine refusal pin — every measure Waves 2–6 claimed would protect the surface.

findings.section: Wave 3 — seed timing / Wave 2 switch_engine relaunch sites
findings.criterion: 1 — POST /api/rnd/term_set_engine switches a live session to and from ChatGPT; the lane seed is written exactly once and the greet arrives
findings.message: First-output-gated seed is specified for `start_session` at `:854-864`. Engine switch is the other way onto ChatGPT that criterion 1 names. Wave 2 applies launch argv at both relaunch sites (`:1546`, `:1692`) and does not apply `SEED_AFTER_FIRST_OUTPUT_BACKENDS` there. Wave 3’s switch GWT asserts `live_sessions()` length and an unchanged `worktree_path`, not that the ChatGPT side was seeded after first output. Toggling Claude → ChatGPT can dump the skill into a composer that is not up — the seed-before-ready risk, on the hotter operator path. Wave 7 then asserts no orphan PTY after toggle, not a seeded greet.

findings.topic: stub engine cmd swallows launch argv
findings.section: Wave 2 — argv order asserted under the stub
findings.criterion: 1 — a terminal opens on ChatGPT with --cd worktree, --no-alt-screen, -s workspace-write; 4 — nothing regresses under ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub + ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD
findings.message: The Codex TUI contract is the launch argv. CI is defined as `ANCHOR_PTY_BACKEND=stub` + `ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD`. Wave 2 asserts the stub PTY’s recorded argv is `[cmd, '--no-alt-screen', '-s', 'workspace-write', '--cd', worktree]` without saying the assertion reads the pre-replacement list `_interactive_launch_args` returns rather than the stub command that actually spawned. If `ANCHOR_ENGINE_CMD` replaces the vector, W2’s new test is green while `ENGINE_LAUNCH_ARGS` never reaches a process, and Claude/Grok “byte-unchanged” pins do not protect the chatgpt branch. Criterion 1 then holds only in the skippable live test. Name the probe point or this is another stub-as-population result.
